author: gobernment
body:
As a former administrator (and really, staff member for 2 years), I've not seen the direction the server has been taking as a tactical advantage for our health. With the infrastructure not being up to the right standard, I have rewritten and restructured all of the network in one policy document, which I have sent the draft to for further review. In this stance, it's been open as a draft for 2 weeks where anyone can suggest changes. As the sole owner of the document, I decided to release some stances of mine to the public. I want to see if all of you would be comfortable with these changes.

​I will be noting certain sentences that may need further elaboration. The only thing I have NOT included for policies is the event team and certain parts of the map developer team, as they currently operate as separate entities (however, combining them as a representation as an "on behalf" of the network wouldn't be a bad idea, either.) I did not include "captain obvious" parts where rank types are stated, or things that come across as legal mumbo jumbo.

​This isn't official! Just words out my mouth.

​

My preface of the document:

  • “The Avicus Network is intended to be a welcoming Minecraft environment, directed towards the audience of teenagers. The primary goal should be straightforward in providing a good moral server with a stable infrastructure for the users (community) to enjoy. Any decisions are to be put in the server’s best interest, for preservation of the community and staff’s health.”

This should effectively stop all attempts to block swearing, and considering the majority of the community is in the age range of 12-19, there should be no reason to bubble-wrap and censor things. I believe making a goal for the server in terms of structure is a necessity, as we constantly strive to meet that goal.

One of the policies state:

  • Transparency is a clear goal of the network. Senior staff (Administrators, Senior Moderators) are to be quick responders and informants to constant arising issues that affect the user base. By any major change, an administrator or senior moderator is demanded the responsibility to make a thread. Staff spotlights are to be held, as well as weekly update posts, also managed by the above ranks. Weekly update posts (or, alternatively, staff spotlights) will be done on behalf of whoever wishes to take on the opportunity.​

One of the policies state:

  • The rule translation project is to include the languages that are relevant to the user base. These would be at this current state English, Spanish, and German. Any other languages may be added, however they are not required to be updated consistently with the others. If a ruleset is outdated past a translation and it cannot be updated properly, in a time frame of 2 weeks, that specific ruleset translation is considered deprecated and removed from the website.
  • If there is an incorrect translation, the senior staff are to forward it immediately to a developer (if the user does not do it themselves). Incorrect translations, minor or major, should be attended to with any available user to translate it. Keep in mind, revising or translation will not be available to users who are not fluent in a language.
  • If the community wants a new language to be added, and they veto for it under proper basis, they may make such a request for the language to where the staff groups are intended to discuss it. Under no circumstance for a translation language request should it be private.
  • A translation team is not recognized officially as a staff group, but a translator group is recommended to tackle the project. The translation project is lead especially by an administrator.

One of the policies state:

  • Moderators who have been demoted are to get a message stating their demotion reason, as well as contact with a senior staff member (to not immediately cut off ties). There are no exceptions. There must be clear cut transparency, and not to “sugarcoat” anything to who received a demotion. 
  • They are to be bound to the same policies that were active when they were staff, and none before or after. They are to be bound under the restriction on that policy revision alone the date of their demotion. There are no exceptions.
  • Senior staff must have evidence and a full confirmation vote before moving on to a demotion stage for the moderator. Majority vote will not be in place, as senior staff should confide in their decision to be absolutely sure, however there can be up to 2 disagreements only. There should be no discrimination against the demoted staff member because of race, sex, party, age, ethnicity, origin, or anything else that is depicted as bias.
  • If a moderator retires, they may receive the retired rank if they served under any branch of staff for a period of 4 months. A staff member is not to pressure a moderator into retiring, however a recommendation / advisement is permitted.
  • If a moderator breaks a rule that coincides with what would be a demotion, the moderator is expected to receive the same punishment as a normal user of the base, regardless of rank. It should be no harsher or lenient. The moderator then is expected to get the punishment, and a demotion if it has been a ban and all parties (senior staff, moderator accused) have discussed it.
  • If a removal of a rank is necessary due to a compromised account or inexcusable behavior that is considered to compromise the server in terms, and you’re sure of it, you may revoke the rank immediately. There is no other circumstances that would go against this policy: you cannot remove the rank immediately if there is nothing breaching the above.
  • All moderators must complete the junior moderator trial first, and succeed. There should be no bias just because there is anticipation for them meeting a higher role.

One of the policies state:

  • Staff warnings are to be distributed to any staff group that is not behaving properly as a staff member, such as not filling criteria or if they are breaking the policy/standards expected.
  • We go off of a three strike system. If you get three staff warnings, you will be promptly demoted. Staff warnings of this strike system will clear every 4 months, however there may still be records kept of the warning. If something warrants immediate termination, this clause is excused.
  • Staff warnings should be managed by senior moderators and administrators via any spreadsheet platform that they consider effective to organize.

​One of the policies state:

  • There are maximum caps in place for the sake of organization and efficiency. There should be no more than 4 administrators, and no more than 7 senior moderators. There is no cap for moderators, map developers. Head map developers cap at 2. Junior moderators should use a batch system introduced so we can keep an eye better on forthcoming staff, in which the limit is 5 and their trial is 4 weeks.

One of the policies state:

  • Suspensions are where a staff member terminates a user’s account, to where there is no way to revert their punishment. This is done under extreme cases, and should be in a long discussion on whether or not to terminate a user. Suspensions are marked with a "@" prefix before banning off of TeamSpeak, the web site, the server, and all other affiliated services.
  • Suspension discussion is to be brought forward to everyone on the staff team except junior moderators and map developers. The one that carries out the suspension should be an administrator or senior moderator.
  • Some of the circumstances of suspension are plugin leaks, heavy exploitation, constant rule-breaking, or breaking the network Terms of Service.

One of the policies state:

  • As a part of using our service, user protection is guaranteed. Staff should never punish anyone for no reason, even at ultimate administrator discretion. There always should be a rule behind a punishment, and to do so otherwise would not be corrective behavior.
  • Staff do not reserve the right to ban anyone without reason. A staff member should be impeached/demoted if this process occurs. There should be no questioning.

One of the policies state:

  • Staff referrals are in placement to where any staff member (excluding map developers) that have been staff for exactly 1 month and over can ‘refer’ or recommend a player for a junior moderator trial. The user recommended must have over 24 hours of playing time, at least 2 pages of forum posts, and be active on a majority of services.
  • They are bound to the same conditions as a junior moderator normally is, except they didn’t get in from applications. There should be a majority vote by the entirety of the moderating team excluding junior moderators, and a template should be used somehow to tally your vote (e.g. a green box provided in the stickied thread).
  • When a referral meets a majority of no, it will be locked. The general rule of thumb is if half the moderators disagree, or there is a very controversial player. That player can be recommended for reconsideration, so as long as they have improved from the thread feedback that denied it last.
  • The user cannot know that they were referred from staff due to confidentiality purposes. This is the only user-related restriction on referrals. They also cannot request a referral.

One of the policies state:

  • For simplicity, there are many things you cannot do as a staff member. This is part of a compiled list of them not covered in other policy.
  • You may not lie to authority, abuse your powers, mislead the community, mislead your fellow staff, break the rules on other networks, be immature, be irresponsible, lead others into retirement, discriminate, be inactive, be disobedient, or represent the server poorly in public. Doing these will result in a staff warning (refer to strike system).

One of the policies state:

  • Reassessment is a system used to reconsider if a staff member has been falsely demoted from the network, or wishes to return. The staff reserve the right to decline any reassessment request for consideration.
  • If a retired staff member wants a reassessment, they are to contact the user relevant to the group (mapdev -> head mapdev, mod -> senior mod), etc. and wait up to a few days for an official response. 
  • If a user returns, they may only return once on that condition. Multiple retirements will not be permitted, and will restrict you from rejoining the team. If a user returns, they are bound to ONLY return as a junior moderator on the moderating team. They cannot join back into their position unless there is thorough error, and the senior staff involved publicly admit/address the mistake for each wrongdoing.
  • If a player does not like the response, they may have a 2nd option where the vote goes to the mentoring team to decide their fate, using a TypeForm document provided by the support email. Responses are to be anonymous. If the mentors decline the return, there is a third option.
  • If a player does not like that second response, they can get a 3rd option. The vote will go down straight to the entire moderator team, outside of mentors, where junior moderators (can’t) vote, but all other moderators can. The TypeForm system will be used, again under the support email. If players don’t like that, there is a final option.
  • If a player does not like that third response, the final thing to do is call for a meeting on TeamSpeak and explain yourself, and host an active Q&A. The moderators will move up, and decide. If declined, you cannot return.

One of the policies state:

  • Policies cannot be edited by senior staff alone unless it is relevant to changing moderator structure, or deals with a department. Moderators are expected to get a vote in all changes to the server, excluding demotions/promotions (which is not relevant to implemented policy).
  • Policies must be enforced at all times, no matter the circumstance. If there is a policy that needs a removal, you should not remove the entire policy, but rather mark it out for later as policies should only be inactive. If it needs to be implemented again, or is only temporary, the clause stays.
  • Policies cannot be made for the benefit of a single user. Policies are intended to help recollect and correct behavior that may take structure off course, affecting the root of all staff groups.
  • Policies are added via moderator majority vote, seniors included in the vote. Anyone can request a policy addition/change/removal by contacting a senior staff member, so community has partial involvement in staff structure.

One of the policies state:

  • If the staff team wishes to run a community event (such as online web browser games or just simple map events), everything must be age-appropriate for someone at least 13 years old. We wish to have content that reflects the moral of the staff team, and this is represented by playing games where it’s not restricted or confined.
  • Events should not be confined to one age group. There is no exception from excluding any member of the community if it’s open game, since as to do otherwise would discriminate that user.
  • Event announcements for the community ran by staff are to have a forum post at least a day before the game (24 hours) so a majority of people have a chance to play.

One of the policies state:

  • Administrator demotions are handled by the owner exclusively. No other user or group may overthrow an administrator.
  • An administrator or senior moderator should be given 3 days before demotion to wrap up projects, prepare posts, clear up things, assist with others in transition, and contribute final works before gone. They are alerted before their demotion, and after the third day, gone.
  • Groups that are formed to assemble and impeach a senior moderator or administrator should be ignored, As shutting them down causes unnecessary drama. If there are valid admin complaints, it should be processed through the owner.

​

So, that's basically my draft for some server changes. Feel free to ask for clarification if you want.

replies.author: gobernment
replies.body:
Excessive swearing is iffy, but I think it should be allowed, in this server environment at least.
Directed swearing is different however, and not allowed.

Also, Avicus cannot protect you from "bad words". You'll find them everywhere over the internet, probably every open website ever. Most of the community is past that stage and the only dislike I ever saw for allowing swearing were the staff teams themselves to appeal to a younger audience -- in which case, our amount of players younger than 12 aren't really "booming" compared to those that are older and do swear. At the end of the day, they're just words.

Excessive depends on the circumstance and context. I would allow someone to say "fucking shit", "shit shit shit",  or whatever, but if it boards into other rules such as spam like saying "fuck" an array of 4 times, no.

replies.author: Zintenka
replies.body:
I agree with pretty much most of this. The staff team does need a lot more transparency and needs to actually warn people before they chose to revoke one's rank. Give the person some time to process at least.

The way demotions are handled currently is absurd and quite angering.

However, I have to disagree with you on the Owner demoting Admin part. While Kylo is the owner and in a normal corporate setting it is the CEO that fires the Manager... Kylo doesn't wish to get involved with staff affairs at all. (Understandable since he is in college. However, it complicates many things such as this.)

However, what would be better is if Senior staff has a specific format for choosing to impeach an Admin. Maybe a separate rank that deals with this. Admins are like Presidents. Sr Staff like Congress.

What if we created a rank that "Interprets" the evidence put forth and hears the Plaintiff's side (Sr. Staff) and the Defendant's side (Admin).

If there are any witnesses (Mods, Normal players, Juniors, etc.) then witnesses must be called when they're online or if they choose to be called (They have the option to stay silent and not get involved if they wish).

The new rank is basically the Supreme Court and it can deal with other staff policies like seeing if a new rule is "Unconstitutional".

If we want an Admin demotion that is well thought out and doesn't take literally overnight... or in a few hours then this is the way to go. A person who holds a considerably high position must NOT be demoted straightaway unless they blatantly did something horrific (Blatant abuse of powers that breaks any part of the server, Racism, Bias, Trolling, etc.)

Things that the admin did that was Mundane and/or didn't have a lasting effect will result in the Admin temporarily losing the position for a week to two weeks. A temporary replacement will be chosen from a vote by ALL staff members (Junior Mods excluded).

The Rank could be called the "Arbiter".

Blatant horrific abuse of powers
- Using commands to alter a large section of a map that severely disrupts gameplay.
- Using TS position to change channel names to extremely controversial names and/or derogatory ones
- Using powers to demote someone out of the blue
- Using powers to intimidate and coerce any person for favors

Mundane abuse of powers
- Using commands that specifically target a very small section of the map or doesn't effect gameplay much (Three day Hiatus)
- Using TS position to change channel names to very silly and/or non-threatening things (Three day Hiatus)
- Using powers to demote someone, however sufficient enough evidence was given. (Week hiatus)
- Anything else that should be considered Mundane through Common Sense. (Varies)
